points: Feed naphtha research octane number was 68.
Reformate research octane number was 92 at a reactor inlet temperature of 510 degrees Celsius, with a liquid yield of 84 percent by volume and an aromatics content of 58 percent by volume.
Higher severity operation at 520 degrees Celsius gave a research octane number of 95 and a liquid yield of 78 percent by volume.
Reactor pressure held at 1.8 megapascals in every run.
Duplicate analysis of 12 reformate samples gave a repeatability of 0.6 octane units.
Octane number fell to 89 after 350 hours on stream at the base condition.
definitions: research octane number = a standardised measure of the knock resistance of a gasoline fraction, determined in a test engine under mild operating conditions
reformate = the liquid product of catalytic reforming, enriched in aromatics and branched paraffins
severity = the combined effect of reactor temperature and space velocity on the extent of reforming reactions
limits: The results cover one naphtha feedstock in a pilot unit with a fixed catalyst charge.
prose: Feed naphtha entered the reformer with a research octane number (a standardised measure of the knock resistance of a gasoline fraction, determined in a test engine under mild operating conditions) of 68. Reformate (the liquid product of catalytic reforming, enriched in aromatics and branched paraffins) from the base condition left the unit at a research octane number of 92, at a reactor inlet temperature of 510 degrees Celsius. Liquid yield at the base condition was 84 percent by volume, and aromatics content was 58 percent by volume. Higher severity (the combined effect of reactor temperature and space velocity on the extent of reforming reactions) at 520 degrees Celsius raised the research octane number to 95 and lowered liquid yield to 78 percent by volume. Reactor pressure held at 1.8 megapascals in every run, and pressure variation contributes no part of the difference between the two conditions. Duplicate analysis of 12 reformate samples gave a repeatability of 0.6 octane units, and the octane gain at higher severity exceeds the analytical scatter by a wide margin. Aromatisation reactions account for the octane gain, and the same reactions consume liquid product through hydrocracking to light gases. The yield penalty accompanies the octane gain at every severity level in the data set, with no condition giving both the higher octane number and the base liquid yield. Octane number fell to 89 after 350 hours on stream at the base condition. The decline develops gradually, and product samples taken through the run show a steady drift rather than a step change after any single operating disturbance. Catalyst deactivation by coke deposition fits the drift pattern, and regeneration planning rests on the drift rate rather than on a fixed calendar interval. The results cover one naphtha feedstock in a pilot unit with a fixed catalyst charge, and a feedstock with a different paraffin content may shift both the octane response and the yield penalty. Commercial units with continuous catalyst regeneration hold octane number near the target by catalyst circulation, and the deactivation pattern recorded here applies to fixed-bed operation only.

points: Influent total phosphorus was 8.4 milligrams per litre and planted-cell effluent was 2.1 milligrams per litre, a removal of 75 percent.
The wetland area was 120 square metres at a flow of 6 cubic metres per day, giving a hydraulic retention time of 5 days.
Gravel bed depth was 0.6 metres and plant coverage reached 85 percent of the surface.
Winter effluent total phosphorus was 3.4 milligrams per litre, a removal of 60 percent.
Unplanted control cell effluent was 5.9 milligrams per litre.
Phosphorus retained over the sampling period was 6.4 kilograms.
Sampling ran for 24 weeks with 3 replicate cells per treatment.
definitions: total phosphorus = the phosphorus concentration of an unfiltered sample after digestion converts all phosphorus forms to orthophosphate, in milligrams per litre
hydraulic retention time = the mean time a parcel of water spends in the wetland, in days
constructed wetland = an engineered shallow bed of gravel and emergent plants that treats wastewater by sedimentation, adsorption and plant uptake
limits: The record covers the first year of operation at one site, before substrate adsorption sites approach saturation.
prose: Influent total phosphorus (the phosphorus concentration of an unfiltered sample after digestion converts all phosphorus forms to orthophosphate, in milligrams per litre) was 8.4 milligrams per litre. Planted-cell effluent held 2.1 milligrams per litre, a removal of 75 percent across the constructed wetland (an engineered shallow bed of gravel and emergent plants that treats wastewater by sedimentation, adsorption and plant uptake). The wetland area was 120 square metres at a flow of 6 cubic metres per day, giving a hydraulic retention time (the mean time a parcel of water spends in the wetland, in days) of 5 days. Gravel bed depth was 0.6 metres, and plant coverage reached 85 percent of the surface by midsummer. Unplanted control cell effluent was 5.9 milligrams per litre under the same loading, and the planted cells removed more than twice the phosphorus fraction of the control cells. Plant uptake and the root-zone microbial community both contribute to the gap between planted and unplanted cells, and the design assigns no separate credit to either mechanism. Winter effluent total phosphorus was 3.4 milligrams per litre, a removal of 60 percent, and the winter decline coincides with plant dormancy and lower water temperatures. Phosphorus retained over the sampling period was 6.4 kilograms, held in the gravel substrate, the plant tissue and the accumulated sediment layer. Sampling ran for 24 weeks with 3 replicate cells per treatment, and replicate cells stayed close through the year, with the seasonal pattern repeating in each cell. Effluent concentration responds to loading within days, and short storm flows pass with a smaller removal fraction than the weekly means suggest. The record covers the first year of operation at one site, before substrate adsorption sites approach saturation, and later years may show a lower removal fraction as the gravel ages. Harvesting plant tissue exports a part of the retained phosphorus from the system, and the harvesting schedule belongs to the operating plan for any full-scale unit built from these results.

points: Initial moisture content of the frozen solution was 78 percent on a wet basis.
Freezing held the shelves at 45 degrees Celsius below zero and primary drying ran at 20 degrees Celsius below zero with a chamber pressure of 15 pascals.
Secondary drying raised the shelf to 25 degrees Celsius and the full cycle took 38 hours, against 46 hours for the reference cycle.
Mean residual moisture was 1.9 percent, below the specification of 2.0 percent.
Edge vials held 2.4 percent residual moisture and centre vials held 1.5 percent, with a standard deviation of 0.3 percent across 18 sampled vials.
Water activity of the dried cake was 0.22.
Reconstitution time was 40 seconds for the new cycle and 65 seconds for the reference cycle.
definitions: residual moisture = the water remaining in the dried product, expressed as a percentage of the dried product mass
freeze drying = drying of a frozen product by sublimation of ice under vacuum, followed by desorption of bound water
water activity = the ratio of the vapour pressure of water in the product to the vapour pressure of pure water at the same temperature
limits: The cycle was developed for one formulation in a laboratory dryer with one shelf.
prose: Initial moisture content of the frozen solution was 78 percent on a wet basis. Freezing held the shelves at 45 degrees Celsius below zero, and primary drying ran at 20 degrees Celsius below zero with a chamber pressure of 15 pascals. Secondary drying raised the shelf to 25 degrees Celsius, and the full cycle took 38 hours, against 46 hours for the reference cycle. Mean residual moisture (the water remaining in the dried product, expressed as a percentage of the dried product mass) was 1.9 percent, below the specification of 2.0 percent. Edge vials held 2.4 percent residual moisture and centre vials held 1.5 percent, with a standard deviation of 0.3 percent across 18 sampled vials. The edge-to-centre gradient reflects radiative heat input at the shelf edge, and vial position contributes more to the spread than any variation in fill volume within the batch. Water activity (the ratio of the vapour pressure of water in the product to the vapour pressure of pure water at the same temperature) of the dried cake was 0.22, and the cake kept its structure with no visible shrinkage or collapse. Reconstitution time was 40 seconds for the new cycle and 65 seconds for the reference cycle, and the shorter time follows the open pore structure left by the faster primary drying stage. Freeze drying (drying of a frozen product by sublimation of ice under vacuum, followed by desorption of bound water) removes the water in two stages with different controls, and the cycle shortens the first stage while the second stage holds the moisture endpoint. Product temperature stayed below the collapse threshold through primary drying, and the endpoint detection by pressure rise agreed with the moisture results at the vial level. The cycle was developed for one formulation in a laboratory dryer with one shelf, and a production dryer with different radiation geometry may shift the edge-to-centre gradient. Scale-up work belongs with a shelf-mapping study on the larger unit before the cycle transfers.

points: Current efficiency was 92 percent at a current density of 450 amperes per square metre, with 55 grams per litre of zinc and 160 grams per litre of sulphuric acid in the electrolyte at 38 degrees Celsius.
Cell voltage at the base condition was 3.4 volts and energy consumption was 3.0 kilowatt hours per kilogram of zinc.
Current efficiency fell to 88 percent at a current density of 550 amperes per square metre.
Cell voltage at the higher current density was 3.7 volts and energy consumption was 3.4 kilowatt hours per kilogram of zinc.
Each condition ran for 24 hours in 6 parallel cells.
Gelatin addition was 0.05 grams per litre in every cell.
definitions: current efficiency = the fraction of the passed charge that deposits zinc, expressed as a percentage of the charge required by the Faraday law
current density = the cell current divided by the cathode area, in amperes per square metre
electrowinning = the recovery of a metal from a solution by electrolysis, with the metal deposited on the cathode
limits: The electrolyte was synthetic, with none of the impurity load of a plant electrolyte.
prose: Current efficiency (the fraction of the passed charge that deposits zinc, expressed as a percentage of the charge required by the Faraday law) was 92 percent at a current density (the cell current divided by the cathode area, in amperes per square metre) of 450 amperes per square metre. The electrolyte held 55 grams per litre of zinc and 160 grams per litre of sulphuric acid at 38 degrees Celsius. Cell voltage at the base condition was 3.4 volts, and energy consumption was 3.0 kilowatt hours per kilogram of zinc. Current efficiency fell to 88 percent at a current density of 550 amperes per square metre. Cell voltage at the higher current density was 3.7 volts, and energy consumption was 3.4 kilowatt hours per kilogram of zinc. The efficiency loss at the higher current density follows hydrogen evolution at the cathode surface, and the deposit at that condition showed rough edges and localised nodular growth. Electrowinning (the recovery of a metal from a solution by electrolysis, with the metal deposited on the cathode) trades production rate against efficiency through the current density, and the operating point in a cellhouse sits where the combined cost of energy and cathode handling reaches a minimum. Each condition ran for 24 hours in 6 parallel cells, and the spread between parallel cells stayed small against the difference between the two current densities. Gelatin addition was 0.05 grams per litre in every cell, and deposit smoothness at the base condition held through the full run with no short circuits from dendrite growth. Cathode deposits stripped cleanly at the base condition, and stripping difficulty appeared only in the rough deposits from the higher current density. The electrolyte was synthetic, with none of the impurity load of a plant electrolyte, and plant liquors with cobalt or antimony carry a lower efficiency at the same current density. A plant trial with recycled electrolyte belongs before any change to cellhouse operating practice.
